P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Fragmented and high-risk. Yemen has two central bank authorities: Aden, aligned with the internationally recognised government, and Sana'a, under Houthi control. They apply competing rules and exchange rates. Since the US redesignated the Houthis as a Foreign Terrorist Organization in March 2025, foreign banks reject Yemen-linked transfers more often and even routine remittances face long delays. This guide covers only lawful routes; it does not describe ways around sanctions.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (permanent residence, at least 183 days, or Yemeni nationals working abroad with income from Yemen) are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents only on income from Yemen. Resident nationals pay 0% up to YER 120,000, 10% to YER 240,000, 15% to YER 840,000 and 20% above; resident foreigners pay 20% (Deloitte 2026). The country is divided, and which authority's rules apply in practice depends on where you live (not researched).

sources.title: Yemen Highlights 2026
sources.quote: Basis: Resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income; nonresidents are taxed only on income earned from Yemen.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Yemen has a general sales tax, not VAT: the general rate is 5%, with 10% on some telecommunications products and services. Companies with annual turnover above YER 50 million must register, and registration is voluntary below that (Deloitte 2026).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (2) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
